name: Hu tieu
summary: Hủ tiếu is the breakfast bowl passed from boat to boat at Cái Răng. Vietnam Tourism’s floating-flavour page says the broth is pork bone and dried squid, with star anise and ginger, and that the bowl has chewy noodles and bean sprouts. The towns page says tapioca noodles, sliced pork, and herbs. Both wordings stay.
origin: The Mekong towns page treats this bowl as Can Tho’s breakfast. It is not the Ho Chi Minh City hủ tiếu.
howToEat: Order it at dawn, on the water, a bowl passed boat to boat.
Vietnam Tourism’s floating-flavour page: pork-bone and dried-squid broth, star anise, ginger, chewy noodles, and bean sprouts.
Vietnam Tourism’s towns page: tapioca noodles, sliced pork, and herbs.
where: The noodle workshops toward Phong Điền are the other place Vietnam Tourism ties to the sheets.
seoDescription: Hủ tiếu from the Cái Răng breakfast boats: pork-bone broth on one Vietnam Tourism page, tapioca noodles on another.
texture: The floating-flavour page says the noodles are chewy and that the bowl has bean sprouts.
The towns page says tapioca noodles. Both descriptions stay.
